correctness.rationale: The integer relation lattice and the common-phase translation group are shown to be exactly isomorphic by two direct calculations: a relation gives v=a-t alpha with constant phase (-1)^t, while a constant phase forces t=v dot beta to be an integer by a carry identity and then recovers an integer relation. A two-copy translation cancellation gives a nonzero bounded Fourier annihilator on sets of arbitrarily small measure, hence failure of L1 uniqueness and all finite-p completeness.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The inspected arXiv:2609.20805v1 states the nonresonance condition only as a hypothesis for its higher-dimensional universality theorem and does not state the converse or the phase-lock group formula. Exact and synonymous searches found no prior statement, and no SCOPE overlap was found. Older simple-quasicrystal sampling and Riesz-basis literature is adjacent but concerns different stability properties. The source preprint is extremely recent, so unindexed contemporaneous observations remain the main residual risk.

value.rationale: The result turns a sufficient arithmetic hypothesis in a new universal-completeness theorem into an exact criterion and identifies its harmonic-analytic mechanism. Resonance causes a sharp qualitative collapse from universality for all sets of measure below one to incompleteness on sets of arbitrarily small measure, while the full phase-lock group and the one-dimensional affine-lattice specialization give structural explanations.
